page.title: Doorbell With Camera and Monitor: eufy E340 + E10 vs SwitchBot, Measured
page.h1: Doorbell with camera and monitor: which kit shows the clearest face indoors
page.desc: A doorbell with camera and indoor monitor, compared on test results: eufy E340 + 8-inch E10 reads a face at 6.7 m vs 2.3 m for SwitchBot. Prices checked today.
page.answer: Short answer. A doorbell with camera and monitor sends the camera's video to a dedicated indoor screen. Best kit: eufy Video Doorbell E340 + 8-inch Smart Display E10. Its camera stayed readable to 6.7 m in LinkdHOME's daylight test, against 2.3 m for the SwitchBot doorbell with indoor monitor.

page.after:
What the differences mean

  • Face distance: 6.7 m ÷ 2.3 m = 2.9. The eufy camera keeps a face readable almost three times as far from the door in daylight (LinkdHOME, same test chart for both).
  • Doorbell battery: eufy used 26% in 30 days (0.87% a day), and SwitchBot used 50% (1.67% a day). 1.67 ÷ 0.87 = 1.9, so on LinkdHOME's test cycle the SwitchBot drained about twice as fast. It died at 47 days, and the eufy was reported off at about 78.
  • Screen detail: 1280 × 800 = 1,024,000 pixels against 480 × 272 = 130,560. The E10 has 7.8 times as many pixels. The SwitchBot monitor shows 130,560 ÷ 2,985,984 = 4.4% of its own 2304 × 1296 camera frame (PCWorld), so the camera's '2K' rating tells you little about what the monitor shows.
  • Price gap: $419.99 − $149.99 = $270.00 for the eufy kit over the SwitchBot kit.
  • Bundle vs separate: E10 at $249.99 plus E340 at $169.99 comes to $419.98, so eufy's bundle costs 1 cent more than buying the two separately today.
  • E10 away from the charger: eufy rates it at over 6 h of streaming, and a battery camera's live view stops after 3 minutes. 6 × 60 ÷ 3 = about 120 full live views per charge. The SwitchBot monitor runs only while plugged in.

Measured side by side: picture, battery and ring speed

David Mead at LinkdHOME tested both doorbells with the same methods. With the test chart in daylight, the eufy E340 stayed readable to 6.7 m. The SwitchBot reached 2.3 m, and Mead notes overexposure in full sun and heavy video compression. At night the eufy reached 4.59 m with infrared only, and the SwitchBot reached 3.3 m in colour night mode.

On battery alone, the E340 had 74% left after 30 days, and the app reported it off at about 78 days. The SwitchBot, on high settings, had 50% left at 30 days and was dead at 47. LinkdHOME also measured 46% human-detection accuracy for the SwitchBot and notes that it has no package detection.

The way each indoor screen answers the bell differs too. eufy says the E10 turns on by itself with the live feed and a voice alert. PCWorld's Christopher Null found that the SwitchBot monitor rings but you have to press play and wait for the stream to load. LinkdHOME timed 5.9 s from ring to live view. On the phone, Expert Reviews' Jonathan Bray measured 6.2 s from a press on the E340 to the alert and 5.3 s more to the live stream, 11.5 s in all. That is slower than the 5.1 s he measured on a Tapo D230S1.

Before you buy the eufy kit: on battery power, E10 live view of the E340 ends after 3 minutes unless you tap play, and hardwiring the doorbell removes the limit. The E10 shows eufy products only. Face and package recognition need a eufy HomeBase S380. eufy asks for a router with at least 40 Mbps download. Once your account has synced, the display keeps working on the home network if the internet goes down.

Not recommended

Skip the SwitchBot kit if your main reason for a doorbell camera is watching for deliveries. It has no package detection, and in LinkdHOME's test it missed 25% of motion events at night. The monitor also does not show the picture until you press play. For a fixed screen that just tells you who rang, it is still the budget choice at $149.99.
